challenges.name: integer-types-and-overflow-quiz
challenges.title: Integer overflow and what compiles
challenges.description: Read each snippet the way rustc does: which arithmetic wraps, which reports the overflow, and which assignments and conversions the compiler accepts.

questions.explanation: 250 + 10 = 260 does not fit in a u8 (0 to 255). wrapping_add drops the bit that does not fit, so it gives 260 - 256 = 4. checked_add reports the overflow as None instead of a number. saturating_add stops at the largest u8, 255. 300_i32 as u8 keeps only the lowest 8 bits of 300, which is 300 - 256 = 44: as never fails and never panics. The explicit methods behave the same in debug and release builds; only the plain + operator changes (panic in debug, wrap in release). Some(260) is impossible because a u8 can never hold 260; 4 None 255 255 assumes as saturates like saturating_add, which it only does for float-to-integer casts.

options.text: It panics with "attempt to add with overflow"

questions.question: Each option is a complete program compiled with rustc --edition 2024. Which of them compile? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: Shadowing compiles: the second let count creates a new variable of type u32 that hides the &str one. u64::from(total) compiles: From is implemented for every conversion that can never lose information, and u32 always fits in u64. let count = 5; count += 1; is error[E0384]: cannot assign twice to immutable variable (variables are immutable unless declared with let mut). let x: u8 = 256; is error: literal out of range for `u8` (the overflowing_literals lint is deny by default). let w: u64 = total; with total: u32 is error[E0308]: mismatched types, because Rust never converts numbers implicitly, not even to a wider type. 7 / 2.0 is error[E0277]: cannot divide `{integer}` by `{float}`: both sides of an arithmetic operator must have the same type, so write 7.0 / 2.0 or convert with f64::from.

challenges.name: load-bags-into-cages-without-overflow
challenges.title: Load bags into roll cages without overflow
challenges.description: The Da Nang depot's scanner stores parcel counts as u8. Write bag_count(raw: u32) -> Option<u8>, which returns None when a scanned count does not fit in a u8 (300 must not become 44), load(cage: u8, bag: u8) -> Option<u8>, which returns the cage's new count or None when the sum does not fit (the runner then starts a new cage), and average(parcels: u32, cages: u32) -> f64, which returns parcels per cage with the fraction. The test runner reads one bag per line, prints the rejected bags, every cage's count and a summary line. It is built in release mode, so a plain + wraps around silently.
